title: Commonwealth Electoral Amendment (Leaders’ Debate Commission) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create a Leaders’ Debate Commission within the Australian Electoral Commission to organise at least three debates before federal elections under independent arrangements.
A commissioner and seven deputies would oversee debate arrangements, with the commissioner deciding formats, participants, moderators, locations, questions and broadcasting details for the events.
The rules would apply to participating parliamentary party leaders and sometimes independent members, with no penalties, and the legislation would begin on Royal Assent.
changes: The Governor-General would appoint a part-time commissioner after consultation with leaders of other parliamentary parties.
Deputies would represent the press gallery, National Press Club, specified political parties and the community.
The commissioner would report within three months after polling day, with parliamentary tabling required.
summary.affected: Participating parliamentary leaders and independent members, appointed commissioners, media representatives and electoral commission staff are affected.
